facts.raw_span: A 62-year-old nonsmoking man presented with multiple pleural thickenings and a marked effusion on the left side
multiple pleural thickenings and a marked effusion on the left side
nodular growth appeared on the mid third of the tongue
Nodular growth observed on the mid third of the tongue
Epithelioid solid formations with pseudopapillary structures
Immunoreactive for calretinin, AE1/AE3, D2-40, Wilms tumor protein 1
Absence of nuclear staining for BRCA1-associated protein 1
Negative for methylthioadenosine phosphorylase
Homozygous deletion of CDKN2A gene by fluorescent in-situ hybridization
Neoplastic subepithelial proliferation, consisting of epithelioid cells in the tongue
Neoplastic cells immunoreactive for calretinin, confirming mesothelial origin
The disease remained stable until July 2023

concepts.why: The patient presented with multiple pleural thickenings and a marked effusion on the left side, and the pathological examination revealed epithelioid solid formations with pseudopapillary structures, which are characteristic of malignant pleural mesothelioma.
The patient developed a nodular growth on the tongue, which was found to be a metastasis of malignant mesothelioma, as confirmed by the immunoreactivity of the neoplastic cells for calretinin.
The patient had a homozygous deletion of the CDKN2A gene, which is a known genetic predisposition to malignant mesothelioma.

The patient presented with multiple pleural thickenings and a marked effusion on the left side, and the pathological examination revealed epithelioid solid formations with pseudopapillary structures, which are characteristic of pleural mesothelioma with a genetic mutation.
The absence of nuclear staining for BRCA1-associated protein 1 explains the diagnosis of BAP1-deficient Malignant Mesothelioma.

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of a nodular growth on the tongue with neoplastic cells immunoreactive for calretinin, confirming mesothelial origin, supports the diagnosis of Malignant Mesothelioma with Tongue Metastasis, which explains both the pleural and tongue findings.
